title: The Current of the Coral Triangle
premise: Astrid Reyes, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vela syndicate, takes a salvage contract from her old rival Marcus Thane: recover a research vessel lost upriver in the Coral Triangle's forbidden interior. The job was sworn off fifteen years ago, after an expedition that killed Astrid's mentor and left Marcus maimed — and the river's source hides a geothermal energy deposit that the Vela family will burn villages to control. As the crew fights rapids, betrayals, and the syndicate's gunboats, Astrid discovers Marcus engineered the whole voyage to weaponize the deposit for himself. In the climax at the source, Astrid collapses the vent system rather than let anyone own it, sacrificing the payment that would have freed her crew. She returns downstream with nothing but her people intact — and for the first time, that feels like enough.
about_author: Cyrus Brightwater is a former marine surveyor who spent a decade charting rivers across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction full-time. He writes adventure novels about people who measure their lives in distances they can never get back.

chapters.title: Debt Measured in Miles
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Chasing a monsoon off Mindanao to earn Vela syndicate money, she reflects on fifteen years of running from the river that killed her mentor. When dockside enforcers present her crew's crushing debt, she accepts a mysterious contract from Marcus Thane. Beat: desperation disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He pitches the salvage job with practiced charm, hiding his prosthetic hand and his true interest in the source. Astrid recognizes the coordinates instantly — the one place they swore never to return. Her crew votes to take it; only old deckhand Suri objects. Beat: the past reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: Provisions and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Outfitting the boat in a lawless port town, she recruits a disgraced hydrologist, Ilya, who knows the upstream gorges. A Vela agent tails them, and Astrid realizes the syndicate expects more than salvage. First nightmares about the drowned expedition surface. Beat: dread accumulating beneath routine.

chapters.title: The River That Bites Back
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The ascent begins: whirlpools, logjams, a near-capsize that costs half their fuel. The crew bonds through crisis, but Astrid catches Marcus logging sonar readings of the riverbed instead of searching for wreckage. Beat: camaraderie forged while trust quietly erodes.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. They pass a village burned to the waterline — Vela gunboats clearing the corridor ahead of them. Suri confronts Astrid: this job isn't salvage, it's conquest. Astrid admits her debt but refuses to turn back, torn between survival and complicity. Beat: guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Marcus Buried
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Searching Marcus's cabin, she finds survey maps of the geothermal vent field dated years before the 'lost' vessel ever sank — he manufactured the wreck as bait. Before she can act, Vela gunboats ambush them at a narrows. Beat: betrayal revealed at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Under fire, Marcus reveals his plan openly: seize the source, sell it, buy back everything the river took from him — including, he claims, Astrid's forgiveness. The crew scatters; Suri is wounded covering the retreat. Astrid chooses the crew over the money, abandoning the salvage fee. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Carrying wounded Suri, the remnant crew reaches the source: a cathedral of steam and turquoise water where her mentor died. Vela forces arrive with Marcus as their guide, each believing they control the other. Astrid stands between them with the vent's fail-safes in reach. Beat: stillness before detonation.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Astrid triggers the vent collapse, burying the deposit under a thousand tons of rock as gunboats are swamped by the surge. Marcus, offered rescue, chooses to go down with his ambition. Astrid nearly follows him into the flood but is pulled out by Ilya. Beat: cathartic destruction and grief.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The survivors drift home on a battered boat with no pay, no debt forgiven, no proof of anything. Vela's claim died with the vent; the debt becomes uncollectible paper. At the river's mouth, Astrid finally stops measuring miles and stays a moment to watch the sunrise. Beat: belonging earned, not bought.
